Wish I could recommend this game because I liked it on PS4 and picked it up on what I thought was a great sale, but the game would not boot for me.  I tried multiple fixes online and in the Steam community hub but none of them worked for me.  DO NOT BUY unless EA ever releases a patch, which they probably won't.

Very disappointing experience

I really wanted to like this game because I’m a big Star Wars fan, but unfortunately I’ve had nothing but problems trying to play it.

First, I couldn’t even launch the game. It simply wouldn’t start and didn’t show any error message or explanation. I spent an entire day searching online for a solution before finally finding something that worked.

Unfortunately, getting the game to launch was only the beginning. Once it finally started, the resolution was completely messed up, and only part of the game screen was visible on my display. At that point, I just gave up.

I’m really disappointed. I genuinely wanted to play Star Wars Squadrons, and it’s frustrating to spend so much time troubleshooting a game instead of actually playing it. I can understand occasional technical issues, but having to spend a whole day just getting the game to launch, only to encounter another major display problem, is unacceptable.

I love Star Wars, and that’s what makes this even more disappointing. I just wanted to sit down and enjoy the game.

Buyer Beware

As of today, June 18th 2026, this game does not boot past the EAC splash screen. EA support is useless and they refuse to address the issue. This review may change if they ever fix it, but I highly doubt they ever will. So right now, do not waste your money on it even on a deep sale.

Edit: The only possible fix that seemed to work was quite literally giving exceptions to every exe file in the game's folder directory in my firewall. Rearlly weird "fix" just to get it to run. Might not be the same for everyone though.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the default flight controls as clunky and poorly mapped, specifically noting issues with yaw and pitch handling.

citations.review_text:
Absolute dog crap controls. They decided to make the left and right on your mouse/game controller yaw instead of roll like a real plane and every other flight game ever made. To make matters worse you can't remap this if you are just using a mouse.

Also having to make an ea account and go online to play a lan round with my son is such a pain that I would return it for that alone. But with the control issue it was a no brainer.

Not only no, but ♥♥♥♥ no. The controls are horrible and clunky. Any sort of advanced or tight movement makes you feel like you're flying a brick. Complex turns will just randomly stop mid-flight, forcing you to press the key again to continue turning. I mean, has all the things i wish i could have snappy fast ships graphics all that ♥♥♥♥.. but the controls are so bad i have to either reprogram my way to old monkey brain, or remap an entire controller.... I remember flying on the og xbox through the training canon on star wars star fighter in the Naboo star fighter... first time i ever touched a controller and i made it through that canyon without a scratch being a dare devil, now i run into things and feel stupid when i reinstall this.

I don't like the fact that I don't like this game very much. No matter what control scheme I picked or customized, the game always felt clunky. If you're looking for a good space combat game, try playing Warframes' Railjack mode. Although it does take some time to get there, it's worth your time if you want a better feeling space combat experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires signing into an EA account and entering an email verification code upon launching.

citations.review_text:
Impressively bad experience. I just got done playing half life alyx again and figured I'd give this a shot since it's been sitting my library for years. When booting up, I'm immediately greeted with a window asking to verify my identity with EA. What even worse is that the UI is bugged. Unresponsive to mouse click and motion controls. I had to google to find out this has been a but for years and I eventually realized I had to tab to select the button. It's just a one time deal though right? There is a "remember this device option" remember? Wrong, it required a verification code to be send to email every time I boot the game up which is absolutely ridiculous. I went to EA's help website and linked my steam account so I could bypass this nonsense. Well that didn't work either. It still greets me with the out of resolution unresponsive "send code" screen and I have to go to task manager to end task to exit out of. 

When I get inside, the game made me incredibly dizzy in VR. Other cockpit titles like elite dangerous do not have the effect on me. Even if it didn't the flying felt horrible. What a crap shoot this game experience has been. I thought I'd ignore all the bad reviews and give it a go. Beware. I requested a refund.
EA 2FA screen comes up during EVERY launch of the game. Unable to get past in in VR, which is the entire reason I got this game on Steam. Quite literally unplayable and it appears EA does not care.

Game is great, everything else is absolute ASS.

You have to verify your EA account EVERY, SINGLE, LOGIN.

Go F yourself EA...

Doesn't work on steam deck even though it's verified. Tried numerous proton versions including GE.
EA account log in is mandatory and text boxes don't line up with the input properly. Took me half an hour to even log in and then there was no sound, despite trying numerous settings changes. Refund requested.

- no frame limit option
- infuriatingly inconsistent mouse input, seems to be dependent on fps, which is bad because no frame limit
- no option to turn of TAA which makes the game look like you smeared vaseline across your entire monitor, even on highest settings
- every time the game starts you have re-enter a 2fa code... wtf
- game needs to be restarted when changing some video settings, which is bad because of the 2fa issue mentioned above

2/10 - All around just a horrible experience. At least it's not as bad as Borderlands 4, so I had to give it two points.

The game just isn't that fun. The multiplayer is effectively non-existent. The campaign is lukewarm at best... And every single time I launch the game on the steam deck it asks me to log in to my EA account. And on top of that I have to use the mouse and keyboard to do all of that but it's buggy and the cursor doesn't line up with where it actually is so you spend about 5 minutes doing that and getting a code to your email every time you load in. I really wanted to love this one but I have to pass.

citations.review_text:
I remember this game being awesome when it came out. Used my flight stick and throttle for the entire story~ I highly recommend playing this with controller and even more so with flight stick.

Now for all of you who bought this and it doesnt launch!!!! i have something for you! 
!!!(USE AT YOUR OWN RISK as you are messing with cpu cores)!!!
each of these should be pasted into LAUNCH OPTIONS 
Copy the inside of the parenthesis
( cmd /c start "" /affinity FF /wait %command% ) This one is 8 cores [as far as i know this one sucks for vr]
( cmd /c start "" /affinity FFF /wait %command% ) This is 12
( cmd /c start "" /affinity FFFF /wait %command% ) This is 16 
I have not tested 12 and 16 cores with vr but hopefully that helps the game run better in vr~
all of these launch the game btw 
I also have the game and the launcher set to admin.

Wish I could get a refund for this.  Don't get me wrong - I played a few hours in between my full time job and juggling my newborn son back in 2021 but the game doesn't even launch anymore - so what is the point?

Games should be purchase > install > play and NOT purchase > install > debug > debug some more > give up for a few weeks > debug even more > browse reddit for hours trying to find a solution > give up > decide to give it another attempt and debug again > wish you could refund since the game isn't playable.

Like what is the point of spending money on something if you don't get the product you paid for?

This game is Incredible once you get it to run, I get that a lot of people do not like the Controls and such but I actually like it, the one thing I don't like about the controls is that sometimes when I try to roll I accidentally change my speed, but that can be changed in the Settings, I also played on Controller which will probably be easier than with Keyboard. My one major complaint about the game is that the game was made with such low Specs that is just refuses to start if I don't limit my CPU to 8 cores and do a whole bunch of stuff because of corrupted stuff. Second complaint is that not enough people play the game in order to play non-solo, AI lobbies
It will not boot unless I manually disable E cores on my CPU.  Only game that has this issue.  I think it's broken.

The old Easy Anti Cheat this game uses will crash on launch on high core Intel CPUs (mostly) 12th Gen and newer. 
I used multiple solutions to launch successfully and reach playable fps or prevent stuttering.

Using Task Manager --> Details tab --> steam.exe --> set affinity --> disable cores starting from last to first i.e deselect cores 11 - 4, not cores 0 - 7 until the game launches, some said 8 cores, I found I needed to select 4 cores. (needs to be done again if you exit steam)

-This is to select your CPU's P cores and to deselect your E cores.  P = performance (e.g. gaming) E= efficiency (e.g. multitasking, web browsing). P cores come first on the affinity selection.  Can use either but not both, the anti cheat doesn't like different strength cores being used at the same time.

Then find the game .exe : in Steam Library --> select the game --> on right side is a cog wheel icon (options) --> manage --> Browse local files --> right click on the .exe files --> properties --> compatability tab --> run in windows 8 compatability mode.  --> then run as administrator.    
(unsure if neccessary, but I also did this for the easy anti cheat .exe)


As for the gameplay, I didn't enjoy trying to fly and target enemies using mouse and keyboard.  The mouse binds to control movement cannot be changed or removed and only one type of input is accepted at once, if I tried using the mouse to get precise targeting while still using the keyboard for other movement,  the keyboard canceled out the mouse.  ... Perhaps lowering the sensitivity for keyboard input would have made it okay for targeting like I needed to turn joystick sensitivity down to 15% to stop overshooting targets.

Using a joystick was great however and I imagine an xbox controller would work fine.  It's worth the discounted price for singleplayer once it's working.  It's really fun if you have the controls set up right and has great performance 60-80 fps on my Craptop.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the multiplayer player base is dead and matchmaking fails to find matches.

citations.review_text:
STAR WARS: Squadrons is the best cockpit EA ever left drifting in space.

Inside an X-wing, every decision matters: power to engines, shields to rear, lasers screaming past the canopy. In VR, it is the childhood fantasy.

Then matchmaking starts searching the Outer Rim for another human.

The campaign is a decent flight school. The multiplayer was the destination. An EA account and kernel-level anti-cheat still report for duty, even when the pilots do not.

Motive built the starfighter fantasy.

EA ejected first.
Really nice gameplay and story, and i like the fact that you get to play with both sides. The player base is completely dead in multiplayer. I havent been able to find a quick play match yet

I feel mixed about this one. Overall, I'm happy I bought and played it because it looks great in VR and it is so thrilling just to see Star Wars stuff in 3D.

Pros:
-Runs super smoothly and...
-...actually looks pretty high-res for VR, which is commendable!
-I like seated VR experiences and using non-VR controllers, it's easy comfort and means I don't fight my headset cable.
-Everything you expect from a Star Wars game (other than Jedi) - high production values, great music, comforting good-vs-evil saturday-morning storytelling.
-Narrative switching between different sides of the same conflict is neat.
-Space lasers go pew pew!

My Cons:
-The gameplay isn't much more than space lasers going pew pew, and I ended up stopping because I didn't like how much it felt like damage was unavoidable in the chaos of a dogfight. To be fair, it's a dogfight simulator, so this one is mostly "just not my taste". Or maybe I just suck.
-They put obvious effort into the characters and writing, which I appreciate, but I also wasn't super compelled by any of it.
-I really dislike the evil-characters-have-English-accents trope, especially when the voice actors clearly aren't English and their accent wobbles.

Cons I Don't Care About But You Might:
-It's a primarily multiplayer game that, as far as I can tell, is dead. I bought it just for the singleplayer, which was fine, but be warned that MP will probably not serve you at all.
-Technical problems. I only experienced one weird CTD, which the Steam forums solved, but I have a great PC and others seem to have loads of issues, including straight up not booting.
-If you want motion controllers in VR, look elsewhere.

5 hours in, I must say, the story is short and BAD.
Gameplay is fun, I might get 20+ hours from this game just for the joy of flying around.
Haven't tried multiplayer yet.

Worth $5 or less.

EDIT: worse than I thought. Couldn't get into any multiplayer match, and solo campaign glitched so could not finish. Still might be worth $2 or less if you have VR or a big screen and just want to fly around once a while.
Good mechanics, mid story, dead online

claims.claim: The single-player campaign features a large amount of mandatory dialogue, briefings, and slow unskippable movement sequences before missions.

citations.review_text:
This is a story mode (campaign) only review, without VR.

Game is beautiful and has great sound. This is the best aspect of the game in my opinion.
The controls feel strange, and I haven't succeeded in finding a set-up that feels comfortable (I've tried with controller and m+keyboard). Flying feels awkward, like I can never do the exact move I am trying to do.

The missions are okay overall, but feel VERY hand-holdy. Many of the missions involve following a squad leader for a fair bit of each mission, which is boring.
Dogfighting is kinda fun, not as fun as I was hoping it to be. There are some cool set-pieces, but II think they are a minority of the time spent.

Between missions, you can chat to your squadmates and leaders of each faction. I personally found the New Republic characters to be rather annoying.
Empire was better, but still cringey at times.

Buy this on sale if you enjoy the visuals and sound of star wars dogfights. There is a magic to flying the faster ships iin first person.
The support ships were a drag for me.

TLDR - Buy on sale if you like Star Wars space battles, graphics and sound great, gameplay mid

Here we have the makings of a great game. But unfortunately, it fell short. 

There are some good things and the most important is graphics. This game is ridiculously beautiful. Like honestly, almost worth picking it up during a -90% discount just to look at it. And it's apparently even better with VR, which I can totally believe. There are also some moments when it feels awesome. Like when you're flying towards a TIE-fighter with your X-Wing and the TIE blows up a second before you collide. In racing game terms I'd describe this as a simcade game, which is kinda cool. You have to choose if you prioritize weapons, speed or armor, for example.

Too bad for every moment like that, you got tons of pure boredom. This game has SO. MUCH. TALKING. Before each mission, you're in the hangar. Someone asks to talk with you. You skip your way through the dialogue. You go to the briefing room. You skip your way through the briefing. Then you're asked to talk with someone again. Skip skip skip skip. Then you go to the hangar, select your starfighter and someone starts talking to you over the radio. Luckily you can start the mission without having to listen to all of this. Then you get a cutscene which is just your fighters flying somewhere and, you guessed it, more talking. After that you finally have control of your ship! Too bad there's nothing to do, you're either slowly flying towards some objective or told to follow the squad leader. And guess what? They talk the entire time!

It's really sad that a game with such great visuals and flight mechanics is ruined by such a broken interface—just try remapping a few keys or a joystick and watch the mess unfold. Lazy development from an irresponsible company (EA) that knew about these issues from day one and couldn't care less about patching them.

Is it fun to play? Yeah... assuming you are willing to adapt to the hardcoded default layouts and push through the various bugs. Support is nonexistent, as expected. It completely pales in comparison to classic titles like X-Wing or TIE Fighter (you’re honestly better off playing the TIE Fighter Total Conversion mod).

A $39.99 price tag for this game is an absolute joke (I picked it up on a deep sale, thankfully). Between the bugs, the total lack of post-launch care, and a campaign that is far too short, it doesn't justify that cost. Considering its age and state, it’s a $10 game... tops.

The old Easy Anti Cheat this game uses will crash on launch on high core Intel CPUs (mostly) 12th Gen and newer. 
I used multiple solutions to launch successfully and reach playable fps or prevent stuttering.

Using Task Manager --> Details tab --> steam.exe --> set affinity --> disable cores starting from last to first i.e deselect cores 11 - 4, not cores 0 - 7 until the game launches, some said 8 cores, I found I needed to select 4 cores. (needs to be done again if you exit steam)

-This is to select your CPU's P cores and to deselect your E cores.  P = performance (e.g. gaming) E= efficiency (e.g. multitasking, web browsing). P cores come first on the affinity selection.  Can use either but not both, the anti cheat doesn't like different strength cores being used at the same time.

Then find the game .exe : in Steam Library --> select the game --> on right side is a cog wheel icon (options) --> manage --> Browse local files --> right click on the .exe files --> properties --> compatability tab --> run in windows 8 compatability mode.  --> then run as administrator.    
(unsure if neccessary, but I also did this for the easy anti cheat .exe)


As for the gameplay, I didn't enjoy trying to fly and target enemies using mouse and keyboard.  The mouse binds to control movement cannot be changed or removed and only one type of input is accepted at once, if I tried using the mouse to get precise targeting while still using the keyboard for other movement,  the keyboard canceled out the mouse.  ... Perhaps lowering the sensitivity for keyboard input would have made it okay for targeting like I needed to turn joystick sensitivity down to 15% to stop overshooting targets.

Using a joystick was great however and I imagine an xbox controller would work fine.  It's worth the discounted price for singleplayer once it's working.  It's really fun if you have the controls set up right and has great performance 60-80 fps on my Craptop.

citations.review_text: I realize this game has been pretty dead for a while.  That being said, even playing against the AI is lots of fun.  There's probably no feeling like a space combat pilot better than jumping into an X-Wing and blasting away the enemy.  Interesting 5-on-5 battle design that shifts focus based on team performance.  Pick this up on sale for cheap and blast away.  Don't expect a big online presence.  There isn't one.

5/10
If this game wasn't so multiplayer focused it could've been the greatest space pilot game out there. However, they chose what they chose. The single player campaign is actually incredible and super fun, but it is also painfully short. If it is on sale, go for it. If not, don't waste your money.

I'll be honest, I bought this game for the single player and have only tried a couple of multiplayer matches. Multiplayer seems mostly dead, but the story missions are fun and fleet battles against the AI are a lot of fun too, though it's a shame the fleet sizes are limited to 1 home ship and 2 cruisers. If you like Star Wars and the prospect of flying in very fleshed out space battles, I recommend it!

honestly not a bad game. Definitely not worth the 30.00$ price tag that it had at release (2020), due to the game lacking updates and being forgotten for more important projects such as Battlefront. Also has a super niche player base with probably 70 people per month on the game, if not less. I purchased the game for under 5$ and I had fun with playing the campaign. It is an arcadey game if it's not obvious, so don't buy it expecting the most realistic experience, although it is actually quite fun with a VR setup along with a HOTAS. My favorite thing to do was to get in a imperial fighter and load it up with missiles and guns. Really the game only has a playable campaign since all the multiplayer servers are dead. But if you like aircraft and space, I'd recommend for you to buy it, just highly discounted.

Wish I could give a mixed rating but positive will do

Squadrons has some solid gameplay mechanics and looks great, and the campaign is fun for the most part. However the multiplayer has been dead for years with no chance of it being resurrected.

Squadrons came out at a time when most people were hesitant to invest their time and money into an EA Star Wars game after EA destroyed their reputation with Star Wars Battlefront 2, and Squadrons looks far too similar to the space combat in BF2. 

I feel like EA let this game down with bad marketing and advertisement as they should've showcased how Squadrons takes the mechanics from BF2 and evolved it into something greater than I expected, like being able to direct power to different areas of the starfighter such as weapons, engine or shields. Also the ship customisation was good, changing weapons and cockpit aesthetics.

It's a shame EA didn't make this free to play instead of abandoning it as there's nothing else like it on the market right now, and I doubt we'll see another game like this in the Star Wars franchise for a long time

Only recommend buying this game heavily discounted for the campaign.

Rating: 7/10

As someone who played a lot at launch online, this game isn't worth picking up unless on a really steep sale, as the online is completely dead (other than through Squadrons die-hard discords) and all that's really left of the game is the single player. Hell, you can't even get credits to unlock gear anymore unless you find a community to do online matches.

But the single player is very good, still. It's very reminiscent of Rogue Squadron from the N64 era, just without the planet locales (the entire game takes place in space arenas). The characters are cookie-cutter, but the story is engaging and makes you feel like you're really, truly part of a squadron for both the Empire and The Rebel Alliance (called The New Republic, as this takes place after RotJ) and the role fantasy is downright palpable. 

So, if you want a really chill fighter-squadrons Star Wars sim, it doesn't get better than this. Avoid if you want more than just a 8-10 hour campaign unless you can find a dedicated flight group online that still runs scrims.
The flying and combat is fun and developed, but the game got pretty much left in the dust with only 1 content update after release. Good luck trying to find a lobby in under 30 minutes.
Very fun dogfighting game. Sound design is great. But it is a dead game now...

This game is great, ignore the negative reviews. This is probably one of the best star wars flight games to ever release. It looks great, combat is fun (feels like star wars), and it even has solid VR support. 

Multiplayer is dead now, but it is still worth it for the campaign and running against bots. Definitely worth getting on sale.

[h2]Squadrons gave me exactly what I wanted: Star Wars dogfights[/h2]

The game understands the fantasy very well: getting inside a starfighter, managing your ship, locking onto enemies, and surviving chaotic space battles from the cockpit.

This is not just a simple arcade shooter. You have to manage power, position yourself well, and learn how each ship handles. At first it can feel rough, but once it clicks, dogfights become tense, fast, and very satisfying.

The campaign is short, but it gives a nice Star Wars military atmosphere, especially if you like pilots, space battles, and the New Republic vs. Empire side of the story.

It can be hard to master, and I do wish there was more content, but the cockpit experience alone makes it worth playing.

If you ever wanted to feel like a real Star Wars pilot, this game gets very close.

Most of folks want this to either be Rogue Squadron or X-Wing/Tie Fighter.
It's neither really but not in a bad way. 
Squadrons offers a surprisingly very enjoyable, not overlong campaign interchanging Imperial and New Republic Missions. It's definitely engaging and kept me hooked throughout.
The Multiplayer was hailed as the No.1 feature and that is where some of the more complex systems come into play, that are barely needed in the campaign and pretty much only have to be engaged with there, if the game wants you to. Among these are power management, Targeting subsystems and DORIFTUUUU.
Sadly, not many people are playing multiplayer these days, though if you can into a classic fleet battle match, they are still great fun with each side featuring one squadron, two corvettes and a capital ship.
That being said, nowadays you can get it on the very cheapo during each Steam Sale and the five bucks it usually goes for are WAY worth it for the campaign alone.

claims.claim: Reviewers recommend using a HOTAS or flight stick setup for the best control experience.

citations.review_text: Remember X-Wing / TIE Fighter from the 90s? I've been craving something modern that comes close to it. I'd settle for close, not exact. Close. This game feels BETTER to me. I use a HOTAS, and it's made all the difference. The key bindings are complicated, but that's how a flight sim *should be*. It's got the Star Wars vibe, the thrill of space battle, and the down-to-the-selector control of managing your fighter's power economics. I love it.
Great successor of the classic, X-wing/Tie fighter games. Play it as it should be played, with joystick or HOTAS.

Graphics 10/10
Gameplay 10/10

If you have the budget to buy some joysticks/throttle (I chose Gladiator NXT with Omni-throttle) on VR or Widescreen.. this game is hours of fun. 

The solo campaign for $5 alone is an insane deal. I look forward to playing multi-player once I get the hang of it. 

Having said that, it has numerous issues that require google searching and trouble shooting.

This game is kind of a decade-spanning satisfaction for me as it mixes the X-Wing and Tie Fighter games of the 1990s with the first-person realism of Star Tours in VR mode (playing this in VR is incredible). The game even works well with an old 1998 Microsoft Sidewinder. Using a flight stick/HOTAS is the best way to play this game, which makes sense if you think about it. Other controllers are much more difficult to use with this game.
The flight mechanics are comfortable and pretty easy to get the hang of. There are plenty of options to customize your ship to your style, though that ability is sometimes minimized or eliminated in story mode, depending on the chapter and mission.
Story/campaign mode is decent but a bit short and some of the dialogue sections feel a bit long sometimes, almost as if to pad the game length a bit. Most of the missions are pretty fun, but on subsequent play-throughs, there's one I like to skip...
The concept behind this game is solid, and the execution is very polished, especially in VR. I would love to see another title in this vein but longer and perhaps set in the core feature film timeline that might allow players to participate in the battles from A New Hope, Empire Strikes Back, Return of the Jedi, etc. Let us fly attack missions the Death Stars, zip on speeder bikes through Endor forests, and pod race on Tatooine!
For under $10, a mixed review, crazy ... well worth the buy, to get the most out of it, I recommend the Thrustmaster HOTAS one.

citations.review_text: Great game for star wars fans, very underrated. Has tons of ships to fly and you can play on both sides of the war, and right now this game really needs players.

You're flying New Republic and Imperial Remnant space fighters, bombers, support ships and interceptors... you manage systems during flight and loadouts before... fast reactions and good aim can be trained. It's Star Wars and you're doing it. Story is enjoyable too. Thanks.

If you ever wanted to jump into an X-Wing (or another ship from Star Wars) and blow things up, this is definitely a must-buy - or if you like Star Wars and flight sims or space sims, it's still a fun game and highly recommended.  The visuals are great, there's a story mode with likeable characters, and all of the flyable ships have quite different characteristics which creates a lot of variety and play styles.

Although I have a full HOTAS setup, many players successfully play it with a variety of control setups (game controller, joystick & keyoard, etc).  It's compatible with head-tracking software (e.g. Track-IR, OpenTrack) which increases imersion if you don't have VR.  It's been out for a while now, and there are definitely some quirks to really getting the best out of whatever ship you choose to fly, especially in multiplayer, but fortunately there are quite a few useful videos on YouTube that explian things - just make sure they came out after the final update, because there were balance updates that significnatly changed flight characteristics along the way.

Make sure to check out the discord communities associated with the game, too.
